items.title: Ruth & Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Saddle River, New Jersey, January 19, 2015
items.q: No but when John was born I was doing an album with Panama Francis.

ctx.x: It took that much, to get to Sinatra.

No but when John was born I was doing an album with Panama Francis. And that day that John was born we had the wrong music for the band that was there. We were supposed to have strings and we had a brass band there. And naturally we had to shift gears you know, and get all the music for the band that was supposed to be on the record, as opposed to what was there. So that’s why I missed the whole birth.
See what he was getting to?

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Billy Bauer from the Woody Herman band, Osie Johnson, Panama Francis played drums, and none of us had those exotic guitars

ctx.x: Yeah. Billy Bauer from the Woody Herman band, Osie Johnson, Panama Francis played drums, and none of us had those exotic guitars they use, that you see on these videos today. We had old fashioned archtop guitars with little Diamond pick-ups on them.
It’s interesting when you listen to some of the early — especially the Chuck Berry records — that he was into the straight eighth note rock & roll thing.

items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 23, 2003 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And we had Jimmy Crawford, Panama Francis, Osie Johnson, they were the best. And we had Milt Hinton and George Duvivier.

ctx.x: In your experience in those days, the racial scene was probably progressing or changing.

Oh it was for the better, because they had the drummers from all the big, good bands, were hired, rightfully so because they were good. And we had Jimmy Crawford, Panama Francis, Osie Johnson, they were the best. And we had Milt Hinton and George Duvivier. The rhythm section were all black. But you never knew it on the record. They didn’t put names on the record. But that was a must. I remember I played a record date one night with Frank Duvall for Tony Bennett, and the drummer was Jo Jones.
Was there a certain place that you guys would hang in between?
